questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the file state that the measures could not wait for the insurer's instruction because of imminent danger (Gefahr im Verzug)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the file state that household contents were stolen or damaged by a theft outside the insured location that was neither a burglary (the thief forcibly entered the building or a room of it, or broke open a container in it, or unlocked it with the correct keys or codes that the thief had obtained by burglary or robbery; a vehicle is not a container) or a robbery (theft under threat or use of violence against the policyholder or a member of the household, or while they could not resist because of unconsciousness, accident or death; pickpocketing and trick theft are not robbery)?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the file state that measures to reduce the loss are still to be taken (not yet carried out)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the file state that the original purchase vouchers for all of the stolen or damaged items cannot be obtained, or only at considerable cost (not even as a duplicate from the seller)?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Is a bicycle among the stolen or damaged items?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Does the policy, or the file, show that the policy does not include the separate supplementary insurance for simple theft away from home (einfacher Diebstahl auswärts)?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Does the file state that traces of the theft (for example pry marks, a broken lock, window or container) have been removed or altered, or are to be removed or altered, by the policyholder or on their behalf, for example by repair or cleaning?

text:
Dear Ms Gisler,

I'll be upfront: I know my household policy with CSS doesn't have the add-on for simple theft away from home. When I signed up in June 2023 the adviser offered it and I said no, to keep the premium down. I'm writing anyway because I'd like to understand where I stand, and whether anything at all is covered.

On Sunday 17 May 2026 my friend Owen Walsh and I went hiking above the Walensee. I left my car at the car park by the lake, locked, with my rucksack on the back seat under a jacket. When we came back about five hours later the passenger window was smashed and the rucksack was gone. Inside were my camera with two lenses, my tablet, my wallet with cards and about CHF 200 in cash, and my phone, which I had stupidly left behind because I'd taken Owen's for the photos. All in all it comes to around CHF 10,800, most of that the camera gear.

I've attached my policy so you can see what I have and where I'm insured.

The cards and the phone were the worst part. Standing at the car park, I borrowed Owen's phone and had my bank block both cards and my provider block the SIM. I didn't ring CSS first because there was no time: the thief already had everything, and within an hour or two he could have been shopping on my cards or running up calls.

The car itself is sorted. The garage in Glarus put in a new window two days later and vacuumed out all the broken glass, so there's nothing left to see of the break-in.

I'd be grateful for a clear answer, even if it's bad news.

Best regards,
Tom Kaufmann
Wiesenstrasse 66, Glarus
